params.body:
## What

A small design system for screens with figures, and the garage's own Inzichten (`/my-insights`, #874) redrawn with it.

**Components** in `resources/views/components/insights/`, with their rules in a `README.md` next to them:

- `block`: icon, title, the answer in one sentence (`answer` slot), then what proves it.
- `register` + `row`: rows in columns, the header once, numbers right-aligned in tabular figures, an optional tail ("En nog 9 wagens."). A row with `href` is a 44px link.
- `meter`: label, groove (8px on a tinted track), value. The label column is as wide as its longest label, so "Meer dan 180 dagen" no longer wraps.
- `empty`: one sentence and one action. It is the block's answer.
- `note`: where a figure comes from, one line in the third ink rank.

**Tokens** in `resources/css/insights.css` (between `@insights-ds:begin` and `:end`, not in refresh.css): a type scale of 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30; three ink ranks from the brand greys (`--brand-ink`, `--brand-gray`, and #667085 from the same grey scale, which reads at 4.8:1 on white where `--brand-faint` reads at 2.6:1); spacing in steps of 4. The page now loads insights.css through `@vite`. Tailwind does not map the tokens: the components carry their own classes, and the Tailwind left on the page (layout, period switch) uses arbitrary values on the same steps.

## The page, block by block

Every block opens with its answer, with the one number that carries it in bold:

- **Bekeken**: "**1.463** keer bekeken in de laatste 30 dagen, het meest via je eigen website." Then a register of the three doors with the date each is counted from (as a column header once, not "geteld sinds" three times), then the stacked chart. "Het meest via" is only said when one door is ahead.
- **Aanvragen**: the same shape.
- **Meest bekeken wagens**: "Peugeot 3008 werd het meest bekeken, **125 keer**." Register: name, views, leads, with an eye and an envelope as column heads so the name keeps its width on a phone. Under each name the views per door as numbers with the chart's swatches, and the conversion where there were leads.
- **Leeftijd van de stock**: "**14 van je 34 wagens** staan langer dan 90 dagen", the last words in amber, which is the legend for the two amber meters. The oldest cars are a register of 5 rows (name, price, days) and "En nog 9 wagens langer dan 90 dagen."; no amber on those rows any more, since there it coded nothing.
- **Verkooptijd**: "Je verkoopt in **29 dagen** (mediaan over 84 verkopen de laatste 12 maanden)." A register of the makes with a median (days, sold), and one sentence for the rest: "Te weinig verkopen voor een mediaan: Citroën 7, Renault 6, ...". Before, "te weinig" and "verkocht" were on every row.
- **Prijsverlagingen**: empty, one sentence with the date once ("Nog geen prijsverlaging sinds 26/09/2026.") and a link to the own stock where a price is changed. With drops: "3 verlagingen op 3 wagens. Na **1 van de 2** werd de wagen binnen 30 dagen verkocht.", the five most recent and a tail. Arrows are written out ("van € 20.000 naar € 18.000").

Bold is gone from names, day counts and subheadings; names are 500, titles 700. Every block has an icon in a fixed 20px box. The icons are passed as full classes (`icon="fa-hourglass-half"`): the theme stylesheet is purged against the blades, and a name glued together inside a component would be purged away and draw nothing. The chart partial moved to the scale too (13 and 11px became 14 and 12, no bold in the readout).

The Dutch page now says "je" throughout ("Enkel je eigen gegevens"); fr, en and de keep their form of address. New answer strings hold markup and are printed unescaped; every value put into them goes through `e()` first.

## Figures unchanged

`App\Support\DealerInsights` is untouched: the same numbers, windows, scoping and valid-from dates. `AGarageSeesItsOwnFiguresTest` passes without changes (its text assertions on "Vanaf", "Herkomst bijgehouden sinds" and "Sinds 26/09/2026" still hold). The page shows 5 of the 10 oldest cars and 5 of the listed price drops, each with a tail; R P2-13.6 and R P2-13.8 say so now.

## The rules as a test

`InsightsKeepTheirRulesTest` renders the page twice (full figures put in the page's cache, and a garage with nothing) and reads it like a lint: every block has exactly one answer sentence; at most one bold element per block, and inside the answer; no middot, no em dash; every `text-[Npx]` on the scale and no inline font-size. It also reads the design system's CSS section: font sizes only as scale tokens, padding, margin and gap in fours, no letter-spacing or uppercase, weight 700 only on the block title and the answer's number; and the four translation files for middots and em dashes. Checked by mutation: a bold make and a middot in the selling register fail two of its tests.

## Checks

- Full suite locally: 2550 tests, OK (own test database).
- PHPStan: no errors. Pint on the new test file.
- refresh.css unchanged, no new window globals; StylesheetSyntaxTest, TheThemeOverrulesEverySpacingClassTest, LanguageParityTest, QualityRatchetTest pass.
- Rendered with sample data at 390 and 1440, before and after, with the purged theme stylesheet as production loads it.

## Follow-up

The "Stock en prijzen" block on Beheer > Inzichten (#871) still uses the older `.ins-card` rules; moving it to these components is the next step to prove reuse. It was left out here because that screen draws its charts with its own script and a paneel behind every bar.
params.title: A design system for insights screens, and the garage's Inzichten redrawn with it
